extracted.intended_audience: researchers and institutions applying for Simons Foundation funding (investigators, postdocs, graduate students, undergraduates, patient advocacy groups, research centers)
extracted.subtask_description: Summaries of Simons Foundation funding opportunities, listing program-specific goals, eligibility signals, priorities, and evaluation expectations across mathematics, physical sciences, life sciences, neuroscience and autism research programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pivot Fellowship: training-year embedding requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The fellowship will consist of one training year where the fellow will be embedded in a lab of a mentor to learn the new discipline and its culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to enable today's brightest minds to apply their talent and expertise to a new field; the fellowship centers on an embedded training year in a mentor's lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simons Graduate Fellowships in Ecology and Evolution: eligibility and preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards provide support for students entering U.S.-based Ph.D. programs with a plan to perform research in ecology and evolution; particularly interested in interdisciplinary research that jointly considers processes on both ecological and evolutionary timescales, or that links…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must be entering a U.S.-based Ph.D. program and plan research in ecology & evolution; stronger interest in projects that bridge ecological and evolutionary timescales or link multiple perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centers of Excellence in Ukraine: foster research excellence and international collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Program intends to continue supporting basic science and mathematics in Ukraine with the goal of fostering research excellence and international collaboration through funding of Centers of Excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitive open call to the Ukrainian research community to fund eight to 10 Centers of Excellence; emphasis on research excellence and international partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Ideas Award: support for bold, exploratory, novel hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide early stage support for bold, exploratory research that tests novel hypotheses and opens new conceptual or experimental directions in the study of autism and related neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD). Proposed research may draw on any scientific discipline, methodology or experimental system (including humans)…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for early-stage, high-risk/high-reward projects; methodological and disciplinary breadth welcome; priority to projects that open new directions rather than incremental work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted Grants in MPS: high-risk theoretical work of exceptional promise
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports high-risk theoretical mathematics, physics and computer science projects of exceptional promise and scientific importance on a case-by-case basis. LOI submission required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rolling letters of intent accepted; program is intended to back exceptional, high-risk theoretical work in MPS with demonstrated scientific importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shenoy Undergraduate Research Fellowship (SURFiN): increase access to research for undergraduates
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal is to spark and sustain interest in neuroscience among undergraduate students who have not had access to research training opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets undergraduates lacking prior research access; programmatic aim is to provide research training opportunities to broaden participation in neuroscience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conferences and Courses Awards (Autism & Neuroscience): alignment with program missions
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding of conferences and courses will prioritize those that align with the scientific missions of programs such as SFARI and other listed programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority to conferences/courses that align with the division's scientific missions and that support activities (presentations, in-person research opportunities) enhancing the research component of meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simons Collaborations (Ecology & Evolution): foster cross-pollination and collaborative groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeks to create strong collaborations and foster cross-pollination of ideas between investigators, often from different disciplines, funding groups of investigators to work together on problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborations are funded to stimulate interactions expected to lead to breakthroughs; emphasis on multidisciplinary groups and sustained collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference Support for Rare NDD Communities: prioritize research component and community focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding intended to support Patient Advocacy Group Family Conferences, with a focus on groups in the Simons Searchlight community, to support and enhance the research component of conferences from scientist presentations to in-person research opportunities for families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open to patient advocacy groups (including well-established PAGs); proposals should emphasize and enhance the research participation/opportunities for families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simons Dissertation Fellowship in Mathematics: support for late-stage PhD students
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides research support to excellent graduate students in the final years of their Ph.D. studies in mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award intended to support dissertation research for outstanding math PhD candidates approaching completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel Support for Mathematicians: stimulate collaboration via travel funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended to stimulate collaboration in the field primarily through funding of travel and related expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports travel that enables collaborative research activity; emphasis on facilitating scientific exchange and partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Software Research Faculty Award: position funding and appointment deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports new research professor positions in existing academic departments to be filled by scientific software-focused researchers no later than September 1, 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award funds faculty positions specifically for scientific software research; includes a firm hire date requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellows-to-Faculty Award: support transition to tenure-track
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports talented early career scientists by facilitating their transition into tenure-track faculty positions through a $600,000 USD three-year faculty research grant, community engagement, mentoring and peer support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus is on enabling career transition with substantial research support and mentoring; eligibility targets early-career fellows moving to faculty roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPARK Research Match Expansion: increase participation of under-sampled ancestries
rubrics_metrics.description: Effort to engage and increase research participation by individuals whose genetic ancestries have been undersampled in clinical research; funding will provide per-person participant incentives for projects that utilize SPARK Research Match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports recruitment incentives (e.g., gift cards) to broaden genetic ancestry representation in research; projects should utilize SPARK Research Match to recruit participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simons Postdoctoral Fellowships in Plant Biology: interdisciplinary candidate preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports candidates intending to pursue a career in basic research on fundamental problems in plant biology; interested in applicants with training in disciplines that could be brought to bear on plant biology, including engineering, computational modeling, …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefers postdocs whose backgrounds bring quantitative or cross-disciplinary approaches to plant biology; emphasis on basic research potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simons Symposia: focused multi-meeting series for interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Brings together mathematicians, theoretical physicists and/or theoretical computer scientists to interact and collaborate in a series of up to three symposia, held every second year and focusing on one topic or a tightly connected group of topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symposia should focus on a specific topic or closely related topics to foster deep interactions across disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2025 Data Analysis Award: leverage existing public datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal is to increase use of large, publicly available data resources by supporting investigators to allocate time and personnel toward working in and publishing from these previously collected data. Applications should leverage existing publicly accessible datasets to ask new questions and extract new knowledge. Priority will be given to applications that…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards prioritize projects that creatively use existing public datasets to generate novel insights; emphasis on feasibility of extracting new knowledge from available data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simons Investigator in Aquatic Microbial Ecology Awards: advance microbial ecology understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for research in aquatic microbial ecology and evolution to advance understanding of microbes' roles in marine and freshwater systems (summary truncated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program aims to fund investigators addressing fundamental questions in microbial ecology/biogeochemistry; applicants should propose work that advances ecosystem-scale understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autism Rat Models Consortium RFAs: recharge and extend consortium research
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants intended to recharge and extend a consortium of researchers using rats as an experimental system to advance understanding of behavioral and circuit neuroscience mechanisms underlying autism and related NDD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support collaborative consortium work using rat models with genetic mutations relevant to human autism; emphasis on consortium-level coordination and advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking Early Neurodevelopment to Neural Circuit Outcomes RFA: interdisciplinary collaboration encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims to bridge the gap in understanding whether and how developmental phenotypes caused by autism risk gene mutation lead to altered circuit formation and function; strongly encourage proposals involving close collaboration between investigators from a range of backgrounds, such as developmental neurobiologists and…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes interdisciplinary teams combining developmental and circuit neuroscience expertise to connect gene-level perturbations to circuit outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SFARI Pilot Progression Award: continuation for projects with significant advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide continuing support for projects initiated during SFARI Pilot awards that have advanced significantly and produced insights that justify an extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended as follow-on funding for pilot projects that have generated promising results warranting further support; selection favors demonstrable progress and clear rationale for extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot Award (2024): early support for exploratory, higher-risk ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide early support for exploratory ideas considered higher risk but with the potential for transformative results, particularly those with novel hypotheses for autism. Particularly suitable for investigators new to the autism field, though applicants are encouraged to consult with experts in autism research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Welcomes high-risk/high-reward proposals and investigators new to the field, but recommends consultation with domain experts to strengthen proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2020 Research Award: prioritize potential impact over risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants intended to provide support for investigation of key unresolved research questions in autism, particularly those that connect etiology to brain function and behavior. SFARI welcomed risk and novelty in Research Award proposals, but potential impact on the autism research field was the most important criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection emphasizes potential field impact as the primary factor; novelty and risk are valued insofar as they contribute to impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel Outcome Measures in ASD RFA: psychometric rigor and scalability
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended to develop and validate outcome measures suitable for intervention studies that target the core symptoms of autism spectrum disorder. Such measures should provide objective data with strong psychometric properties, be scalable for use in large, multisite studies, not be unduly burdensome to participants and…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should prioritize objective, quantitative measures with proven psychometric strength and feasibility for large-scale multisite trials while minimizing participant burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPARK Clinical Site Network RFA: build a representative research cohort
rubrics_metrics.description: SPARK is intended to recruit, engage and retain a community of 50,000 individuals with autism and their family members in the United States, spanning the full autism spectrum and individuals of all socio-demographic backgrounds. This RFA supported additional U.S.-based clinical sites for the cohort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites should contribute to recruitment, retention, and representativeness of the cohort across ages and sociodemographic backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genomic Analysis for Autism Risk Variants in SPARK: encourage innovative analysis of large family datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants intended to advance understanding of the genetic basis of autism by analyzing genomic data in innovative ways from thousands of SPARK families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should propose novel analytical approaches to leverage large familial genomic datasets to discover autism risk variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explorer Awards: fund exploratory experiments to strengthen hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended for proposals requesting support of exploratory experiments that will strengthen hypotheses and lead to formulation of competitive applications for subsequent larger-scale funding. Innovative, high-risk/high-impact proposals were encouraged and applications from investigators new to the field were especially encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed at short-term, hypothesis-strengthening experiments that make later large-scale proposals more competitive; welcomes applicants new to autism research with complementary expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole-Genome Analysis for Autism Risk Variants: focus on non-coding and less-accessed regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended to advance understanding of the genetic basis of autism, in particular to begin to assess genetic variants conferring risk in non-coding regions and in coding regions of the genome that may be less accessible to whole-exome sequencing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages development of innovative, efficient analytical methods to interrogate non-coding and hard-to-assay coding regions for autism risk variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional Screen of Autism-Associated Variants RFA: medium/high-throughput functional testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended to advance understanding of the potential role of missense and in-frame deletion variants in conferring risk; investigators interested in developing medium- or high-throughput screens to test the functional effects of such variants were encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes scalable functional assays that can systematically evaluate variant effects; suitability for medium- to high-throughput workflows is desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innate Immune System Impact RFA: physiologically relevant immune activation/inhibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants intended to advance understanding of the impact of activation of the innate immune system on behavioral, circuit, synaptic and neuronal functions. Experiments were expected to include physiologically relevant activation/inhibition of the innate immune system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for studies using physiologically relevant immune manipulations and measuring downstream neural and behavioral consequences relevant to autism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circuit Dynamics RFA: determine downstream consequences of genetic perturbations on circuitry
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended to advance understanding of the circuit basis for behavioral and cognitive alterations relevant to autism spectrum disorders (ASD), with the goal of determining the downstream consequences of autism-associated genetic perturbations on neural circuitry and coordinated neuronal activity during autism-relevant behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports studies linking genetic perturbations to circuit-level function during behavior; emphasis on mechanistic circuit analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of Simons VIP Biospecimens RFA: comprehensive RNA-expression characterization tied to phenotype
rubrics_metrics.description: Sought proposals that take advantage of biospecimens and rich phenotypic information collected by Simons VIP, giving priority to approaches that aim to accomplish a comprehensive characterization of RNA expression differences and correlate such expression patterns with phenotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority to integrative analyses combining molecular expression profiling with phenotype correlations; proposals that further analytic capabilities and phenotype integration favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mouse Phenotyping RFA: testing multiple genetic models in consistent background
rubrics_metrics.description: Aimed to comprehensively analyze behavior of mouse models generated with targeted genetic mutations based on strong human genetic evidence implicating them in ASD. Investigators were expected to test at least three genetic models in the same background strain (C57BL/6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires testing of multiple (>=3) genetic models under a common background strain to ensure comparability; emphasis on models grounded in human genetic evidence and comprehensive behavioral analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-level priorities: interdisciplinary collaboration and translational potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Across multiple RFAs and programs, there is recurrent emphasis on interdisciplinary collaboration (e.g., between developmental neurobiologists and circuit scientists), multidisciplinary teams (human + animal expertise), and potential for translational outcomes (biomarkers, interventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should assemble teams with complementary expertise, aim for translational relevance where indicated, and design studies that bridge levels (molecular → circuit → behavior) when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for innovative, high-risk/high-impact proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple programs explicitly welcome or prioritize bold, innovative, high-risk/high-impact research that opens new conceptual or experimental directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk and novelty are valued when accompanied by potential for substantial impact; several mechanisms exist specifically to support exploratory or high-risk projects.
